$comment: Static transitive dependency manifest. Built by grepping the actual generalized skill files for real cross-references (process/skills/*/SKILL.md), not from memory of the source repo. 'hard' means the skill's own documented steps invoke the target and have no stated fallback; 'soft' means the skill explicitly states a fallback ('if X isn't installed, do Y yourself') or the reference is a pipeline-stage pointer to a genuinely optional next step. All hard skill-to-agent edges are satisfied automatically for any adopter who installs process/ as the integrated shelf intends, since code-reviewer and docs-writer ship as part of that same shelf - they only matter if a component is cherry-picked out of process/ on its own.

design-gate.notes: execution-gate/implement-queue/backlog are pipeline-stage pointers to genuinely optional next steps. execution-gate specifically: design-gate's own Step 3.5 makes considering it a mandatory, recorded checkpoint for substantial designs, but running it always stays the adopter's own optional call.

execution-gate.notes: Planning-phase skill - it recommends which bucket (main model / docs-writer / code-reviewer / fork) each task should use, it doesn't invoke them itself. Hard edge reflects that its output is meaningless without those agents existing to delegate to.

external_prerequisites.name: Workflow tool with worktree support
external_prerequisites.note: D3 (build spec section 0): no reduced sequential mode is shipped. The skill and the process/workflows/implement-queue.js script both assume this is available; state the precondition in the README rather than building a second implementation.

implement-queue.notes: The .js workflow script (process/workflows/implement-queue.js) sets agentType: 'code-reviewer' / 'docs-writer' directly in its own agent() calls - confirmed by reading the built file, not inferred. design-gate/backlog are hard here because this skill's own checklist mechanism is meaningless without the upstream skills that populate and gate it. execution-gate is soft, not hard: running it always stays optional (its own SKILL.md and docs/WORKFLOW.md section 4 both state this - only considering it is a mandatory, recorded checkpoint in design-gate Step 3.5, not the run itself), and its output is never what populates a BACKLOG.md checklist entry - that's design-gate's job alone. implement-queue reads an execution-strategy section if one exists but works correctly without it.

commit.notes: Companion/contrast relationship only ('lightweight companion to wrap-up-session') - no functional call from commit into wrap-up-session. Works standalone.

handoff.notes: context-usage-nudge is standalone-shelf, not process-shelf - this is the one real process-to-standalone soft edge in the export. The skill's own text: 'if you have one wired up' - fully functional without it, just loses the automatic trigger.
